history: First measured with the fixture reaching (1, 0, 2) against a corpus reaching (5, 2, 2): every shared obligations handler carried its route decorator, so nothing in the suite exercised a handler registered from another document, and no chain was longer than one binding. `from_spec` was added to the fixture to close that, and it is the connexion shape the vibe-py rows really have.
note: learning-harness Req 10.4. Higher is harder on every axis. `binding_hops` counts the assignments between the identity source and the constrained use; `registration_distance` is 0 for a route decorator on the handler, 1 for a statement elsewhere in the same file, 2 for another document entirely; `guard_distance` is 0 for a decorator guard, 1 for a call in the body, 2 for no visible guard. The comparison is per axis over the whole set: a suite covers a bug shape with several handlers between them, but its hardest case on an axis must not fall short of the corpus rows its tests claim to cover.
